Glossary

The ERCOT queue is a technical document. A few dozen acronyms and phase names show up across the map, filter sidebar, project pages, and API. Here's what they mean, in plain English.

◆ AI / data-center flavored
A soft classification used on the map and movers page. Flagged when theinterconnecting entity (developer/owner name) matches a curated list of operators clearly connected to the AI/data-center theme —CleanAI, LLC, Kalnin Ventures, LLC,Palomino Alpha, LLC, Bullock Data Center, LLC,Liberty Data Center I, LLC — or when the entity name simply contains "Data Center". This is soft evidence, not proof: the queue doesn't disclose end-customers. But when developers named "Data Center, LLC" file 1.4 GW gas plants, the pattern is worth surfacing. Toggle the sidebar checkbox to filter the map to just these.
BESS
Battery Energy Storage System. Grid-scale batteries. In the ERCOT data they show up under fuel code OTH with technology BA. They're the dominant category by project count — 881 of the 1,827 projects in the current queue.
CDR Zone
Capacity, Demand and Reserves reporting zone. ERCOT divides Texas into six regions — HOUSTON, NORTH, SOUTH, WEST, PANHANDLE, COASTAL — used for planning and reserve tracking. Every project is tagged with one.
COD
Commercial Operation Date. The target date a project expects to start generating power for the grid commercially. Slips are the norm — 126 projects slipped their COD in the July 2026 report alone, totaling 24 GW of delayed capacity.
ERCOT
Electric Reliability Council of Texas. The grid operator for most of Texas. Publishes the monthly GIS report this site is built on.
Fuel code
Three-letter code for a project's primary energy source. Common values:SOL (solar), WIN (wind), GAS (natural gas),OTH (other — mostly batteries), NUC (nuclear),WAT (hydro).
FIS
Full Interconnection Study. The deeper of the two grid-impact studies ERCOT performs on a proposed project. Follows the screening study. Can take a year or more; when it completes, the project is close to being able to sign an Interconnection Agreement.
GIM
Generation Interconnection or Modification. ERCOT's umbrella term for the process of connecting new generation to the grid. The "GIM Study Phase" column summarizes where each project is in that process.
GIS report
Generator Interconnection Status report. The public monthly Excel workbook ERCOT publishes atercot.com/gridinfo/resource. Roughly 1,800 rows, one per proposed project. The raw source for this site.
IA
Interconnection Agreement. The signed contract between a project and ERCOT/the transmission owner that authorizes the project to physically connect to the grid. Major late-stage milestone; once signed, the project is likely to get built.
INR
Interconnection Request Number. The unique identifier assigned to every project when it enters the queue. Format isYYINR#### — the first two digits are the year the request was filed (e.g. 26INR0546 was filed in 2026).
MW / GW
Megawatt / Gigawatt. Units of electrical power (not energy). 1 GW = 1,000 MW. A large nuclear reactor is about 1 GW. Texas peak summer demand runs around 85 GW. The ERCOT queue totals roughly 440 GW of proposed capacity.
POI
Point of Interconnection. The specific substation or transmission line where a proposed project would physically plug into the grid. Shown on each project's detail page.
Screening Study (SS)
The first, faster study ERCOT performs on a new project — a preliminary check for feasibility. Projects that pass move on to the Full Interconnection Study.
Technology code
Two-letter code for how a plant generates electricity. Common values:PV (photovoltaic solar), WT (wind turbine),CC (combined-cycle gas), GT (gas turbine),IC (internal combustion), BA (battery).
Withdrawn
A project has been removed from the queue — either the developer canceled it or ERCOT dropped it for missing milestones. Distinct from a project that completes and becomes operational. In the current report, 31 projects were withdrawn since the prior month, totaling 5.6 GW.

What this shows

Every power plant proposed in Texas — from a 5-megawatt battery to a 1.5-gigawatt gas plant — first appears in one place: the ERCOT Generator Interconnection Status queue. It's a monthly Excel file, buried on ERCOT's website, listing 1,800+ projects. It's the earliest signal of what will actually be built — years before permits, press releases, or news coverage.

This site downloads that file every month, diffs it against the prior month, and surfaces what changed.

What's in the queue right now

440 gigawatts of proposed generation are waiting to plug into the Texas grid. For scale: Texas peak demand last summer was about 85 GW. What's proposed here is roughly five years of the entire state's electricity supply. Most of it will never be built — but tracking which projects advance, slip, or vanish is how you see the Texas grid buildout in real time.

What changed in the July 2026 report

  • 30 new projects entered the queue (11.2 GW proposed)
  • 31 projects were withdrawn (5.6 GW removed)
  • 126 projects slipped their target completion date (24.3 GW affected)
  • 35 projects advanced through screening or study milestones
  • 20 projects changed hands

The month's biggest story: nine of the new gas plants — from Kalnin Ventures (2 × 1,273 MW in Jack County), Palomino Alpha (5 × 400 MW in Guadalupe County), and a developer literally named CleanAI, LLC (2 plants in Freestone County) — total 4.5+ GW of new gas proposed in a single month. Names like these are the signature of AI-data-center-driven load growth showing up in the physical grid.

Three things to look at right now

  • Bullock Gas — 1.4 GW gas plant owned by Bullock Data Center, LLC. Entered the queue in June, already advanced through screening study by July.
  • Thunder Bird 2 Gas — one of two identical 1,273 MW gas plants from Kalnin Ventures, both filed in July in Jack County.
  • Lost Pines Power Park — 880 MW gas plant that just pushed its target online date from Dec 2030 to Jun 2033. A two-and-a-half-year slip in one report.

Data source

Raw data: ERCOT GIS Report. Downloaded monthly, parsed from Excel, stored in SQLite. Not affiliated with or endorsed by ERCOT. Public data, used under ERCOT's open data policy.

JSON API

Everything you see is queryable as JSON. Freely usable for non-commercial reporting and analysis.

GET /api/summary                             # dashboard stats
GET /api/projects?fuel=SOL&min_mw=100         # filtered project list
GET /api/projects/{'{'}inr{'}'}                       # single project + change history
GET /api/movers?change_type=NEW              # this month's biggest movers
GET /api/filters                             # dropdown values

Example: biggest new gas plants this month

curl /api/movers?change_type=NEW | jq '.movers[] | select(.fuel=="GAS") | {name, mw: .capacity_mw, entity: .interconnecting_entity}'

Example: every COD slip above 500 MW

curl "/api/projects?change_type=COD_SLIPPED&min_mw=500&changed_since=2026-06-01"

Refresh cadence

Rebuilt monthly from the latest ERCOT report via GitHub Actions cron (7th of each month, after ERCOT typically publishes). This snapshot is from July 2026.

Built

Candid Intelligence Hackathon, Houston, August 2026. Python + SQLite + FastAPI + Astro + MapLibre GL JS.
